newsitem.title: UK: Euro straight-run deal heard at $110-$112 a tonne.
newsitem.headline: Euro straight-run deal heard at $110-$112 a tonne.

text.p: Euro straight-run fuel remained buoyant on Friday, with a private and confidential deal for standard low sulphur material heard done at a heady $110-$112 fob a tonne, traders said.

The Scandinavian material, due to load August 15-20, was boosted by short supply in the European market and solid demand for residual fuels on both sides of the Atlantic despite problems at large catalytic crackers in both locations.
The last low sulphur deal, a week ago, was done at $109.25 a tonne.

Russian high sulphur was also sought after, though not as ferociously as a week ago. M100 cargoes were fetching premia of $4 or $5 above the two means and E4 vessels were priced $2-$3 over the three means.
